region: Hector · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Chateau LaFayette Reneau was founded in 1985 on the east shore of Seneca Lake, in the town of Hector, by Dick Reno, and its tasting room occupies a fully restored, century-old barn above the water. The 110-acre estate faces west over the lake, whose depth tempers the climate on its slopes. Since late 2013 the winery has been owned by Gene Pierce, who also owns Glenora and Knapp, and its long-serving winemaker, Tim Miller, has guided the cellar for more than two decades.

Riesling has long been the winery’s signature. Its Rieslings have won New York’s Governor’s Cup several times, including the 1997 Johannisberg Riesling and, in 2014, a Semi-Dry Riesling from the 2013 vintage made in Pierce’s first harvest as owner. The Semi-Dry is made without oak and keeps a measure of the grape’s natural sweetness, balanced by the bright acidity that the cool Finger Lakes climate gives Riesling.

The winery’s notes describe Meyer lemon, fresh apricot and ripe banana on the nose, a round, lively, light-to-medium body, and a smooth finish touched with custard tart and brûléed lime. There is no oak to soften the fruit, so the wine stays bright and fresh from start to finish. With its gentle sweetness and lift, it is a natural partner for spice, smoke and the char of a wood fire.
